name: Ramp
text:
Add a single high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that only appears when focused.

This solves the keyboard navigation problem cleanly: users can bypass repetitive blocks without cluttering the interface. The trade-off is one extra tab stop, but it’s a small price for universal access.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is sighted keyboard users will still overlook the skip link—sighted keyboard users treat them as invisible until they’re forced to notice them. A persistent skip link that’s always visible (but subtle) avoids this trap while keeping the benefit for screen-reader users. Test with both keyboard-only and screen-reader users to settle it.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **persistent, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, always visible but subtle—like a thin, colored bar—so sighted keyboard users notice it without extra tab stops. Screen-reader users get the same benefit without confusion, and the link never disappears. The trade-off is a tiny bit of visual weight, but universal access outweighs minimal clutter.

name: Reader
text: The real risk is that a persistent skip link still risks blending into the page’s visual noise—sighted keyboard users may skip it if it’s not *immediately* attention-grabbing. A better alternative: make the skip link a **bold, full-width button** that appears *only* when tabbed into, then fades back to a subtle indicator. Settle it with A/B testing: track how often sighted keyboard users actually use it versus screen-reader users.
